playbooks.name: Pick one thing and mean it
playbooks.blurb: The commonest first mistake is launching with fifty products. Depth beats breadth — prove one thing sells before you widen.

playbooks.name: Make it buyable
playbooks.blurb: Most sellers wait until everything is perfect before telling anyone the shop exists. Get it buyable, then improve it in public.

playbooks.name: Prove it before you pay
playbooks.blurb: Word of mouth and a social presence drive most first-year growth. Paid ads accelerate something that already works — they cannot create it.

playbooks.name: The first ten customers
playbooks.blurb: The first ten buyers get found one at a time, by hand. Nothing at this stage scales, and trying to make it scale is why people quit.

playbooks.name: Test without burning cash
playbooks.blurb: If you ever run ads: decide the kill number before you spend, not after. A product gets a fixed budget and a deadline, then it lives or it dies.

milestones.title: Open the Discover feed
milestones.detail: See what's worth selling right now, and what it costs to source.

milestones.title: Open a product that catches your eye
milestones.detail: Tap a card for the cost, the resale price, and the case for it.

milestones.title: Try the Maker and Seller filters
milestones.detail: Two different businesses. Maker means you make it; Seller means you source it and resell it.

milestones.title: Bookmark something
milestones.detail: Tap the heart on a product. It lands in Business → Bookmarks so you can come back to it.

milestones.title: Open your journey
milestones.detail: This list. Every step between here and your first sale.

milestones.title: Pick your niche
milestones.detail: Choose one. You can change it later — but pick one now rather than three.

milestones.title: Find where to source it
milestones.detail: Open the sourcing link on your product and see the real unit cost.

milestones.title: Price three real competitors
milestones.detail: Search your product on Etsy or eBay and write down what three actual sellers charge. Not what you hope to charge.

milestones.title: Work out what you actually keep
milestones.detail: Unit cost, shipping, packaging, platform fee — subtract all of it from your price. That number is the business. If it is under a third of your price, change something now rather than later.

milestones.title: Name your business
milestones.detail: A name you can say out loud without wincing. It does not have to be clever.

milestones.title: Start your business
milestones.detail: Mark the day you decided. It matters more than it sounds.

milestones.title: Order one for yourself
milestones.detail: Buy your own product before you sell it. You find out what the photos hide, how long shipping really takes, and what turns up in the box.

milestones.title: Open a place to sell
milestones.detail: Etsy, Shopify, a marketplace, or an Instagram account with a checkout link. Anywhere someone can actually pay you.

milestones.title: Take your first product photos
milestones.detail: Daylight, plain background, one shot that shows scale. A phone is fine — lighting is what separates a listing that sells from one that does not.

milestones.title: Answer the objection in your listing
milestones.detail: Name the reason someone would hesitate — size, shipping time, whether it is really handmade — and answer it in the description. Most listings sell; the ones that convert reassure.

milestones.title: List your first product
milestones.detail: One product, listed and live. Not five. One.

milestones.title: Put it on your shelf here
milestones.detail: Business → Money → The shelf. Keeps your prices and stock in one place.

milestones.title: Open the Grow feed
milestones.detail: The places the people who buy what you make already gather.

milestones.title: Find a community for your niche
milestones.detail: Open one and read the profile — what they discuss, what wins them over, what gets you removed.

milestones.title: Read it for a week before posting
milestones.detail: Every community here has a rules section, and the fastest way to get banned is to arrive selling. Lurking costs a week and saves the account.

milestones.title: Focus on one community
milestones.detail: One room you show up in properly beats five you drop links into.

milestones.title: Introduce yourself there
milestones.detail: Not a pitch. Answer somebody's question, or show what you are making and how.

milestones.title: Add where your business lives
milestones.detail: You → Socials. One place people can find you is enough to start with.

milestones.title: Add your first person
milestones.detail: Business → Clients. Anyone who showed interest, not only people who bought.

milestones.title: Log a conversation
milestones.detail: Every time you talk to someone, log it. Their relationship strength rises, and it tells you who is worth following up.

milestones.title: Make your first sale
milestones.detail: Somebody paid you. Everything before this was preparation.

milestones.title: Log your first sale
milestones.detail: Business → Money. Record what sold, for how much, and to whom.

milestones.title: Ask your buyer to tell one person
milestones.detail: Word of mouth is the biggest growth channel in a first year. One sentence once they have it: if you like it, tell somebody. Most people will.

milestones.title: Log five sales
milestones.detail: Five is where you stop guessing. You start seeing which product, which channel, and which kind of buyer.

milestones.title: Set a test budget before you advertise
milestones.detail: If you go paid: pick a fixed number per product and stop there. Sellers who test properly give one product a few hundred and no more.

milestones.title: Decide the kill number first
milestones.detail: Write down what a customer may cost before the sale stops being worth making — roughly under 40% of your profit per unit. Decide it before you spend, because afterwards you will argue with yourself.

milestones.title: Test one product properly
milestones.detail: One product, the budget you set, the kill number you wrote. Then honour it — scale it or drop it, no exceptions.

milestones.title: Give it ninety days
milestones.detail: First sales take weeks or months. Most shops that fail close before they were ever really tested. Mark a date ninety days out and do not judge it before then.

milestones.title: Find a second thing to sell
milestones.detail: Only now. One proven product first, then widen — not the other way round.
